test_title: RRB NTPC CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 21 Jan 2021 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: Name the Viceroy of India who was associated with the controversial Ilbert Bill during the Indian freedom struggle.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Lord Ripon**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Sir Courtney Pergine Ilbert, **a law member of the Viceroy's council, authored the Ilbert Bill during Lord Ripon's viceroyship in 1883.
 
• It was recommended that top Indian magistrates preside over matters involving British personnel in India.
 
• Owners of British tea and indigo estates in Bengal were vehemently opposed to the bill. In reaction to the popular condemnation of the Ilbert Bill by a majority of English women, Viceroy Ripon (who had introduced the Bill) passed an amendment mandating a jury of 50% Europeans if an Indian judge was to face a European on the dock.
 
• During the Viceroyalty of the Marquess of Ripon, Sir Courtenay Peregrine Ilbert, a valid member of the Council of the Governor-General of India, prepared the Ilbert Bill, which was formally tabled on 9 February 1883.
 
• The Ilbert Bill was named after Courtenay Ilbert's "Bill to alter the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1882, so far as it relates to the exercise of jurisdiction over European British persons." 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Lord Dufferin** served as Governor-General of India and Viceroy from **1884 to 1888**. During his tenure, the Third Burmese war led to the annexation of the whole of Burma, and the Burmese ruler was exiled to India. **In 1885, AO Hume laid the foundation of the Indian National Congress.**
 
• **Lord Mayo** or **Lord Naas** served as **4th Viceroy of India** from **12 January 1869 to 8 February 1872**. He started the process of decentralization of finance. In foreign affairs, he followed the policy of non-intervention. He opened up Mayo College in Ajmer for educating children of aristocratic families. India’s census began during his tenure. He was the first Governor-General to be murdered in office by a Pathan Sher Ali in Port Blair.
 
• **Lord Lansdowne** served as Governor-General and Viceroy of India from **1888 to 1893**. During his tenure, the Indo-Afghan border {Durand Line} was demarcated. The Indian Council Act of 1892 was enacted and a system of indirect elections started in India.
